title: Design System: Fisher Lok Precision Calibration Console

section-title.purpose: Large section signposts for projects and writing.

label.purpose: Uppercase metadata, stage indices, and compact readouts.

link.purpose: Uppercase project, journey, and blog links.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Navigation, controls, border/background, and link state changes.

motion.name: evidence-reveal
motion.purpose: Panel content reveal using opacity, clip-path inset, and an 8px upward settle when a journey tab changes.

motion.name: media-settle
motion.purpose: Subtle project-media response on row hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Scroll behavior becomes auto and all transitions/animations are reduced to 0.01ms; evidence reveal is not added.

breakpoints.name: tablet-tight
breakpoints.purpose: Tighten hero, move journey links below copy, and move blog links beneath titles.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Two-row navigation, stacked hero, 2×2 journey tabs, vertical projects, and stacked contact.

breakpoints.name: small-mobile
breakpoints.purpose: 20px gutters, compact action grid, stacked journey heading, 42px project rows, and block blog entries.

narrative.overview:
The interface treats engineering evidence as a calibrated signal path. Cool-white and midnight surfaces, graphite type, cobalt state color, instrument-grade lines, and compact mono readouts make the progression from research to reliable trading systems legible without pretending to be a trading terminal. The visual world is quiet at rest and exact in state: hierarchy comes from scale, alignment, contrast, and evidence, not ornament.

The portfolio opens with a large identity statement and direct conversion actions, then gives the visitor a four-stage Research → Data → Execution → Monitoring control. Projects are evidence rows with real imagery, descriptions, tags, and links; the blog is a dark, structured reading list; contact resolves into a high-contrast cobalt field. Light and dark modes share the same geometry and state logic.
keyCharacteristics: Calibrated signal-path storytelling from research to monitoring.
Cool-white and midnight tonal surfaces with cobalt reserved for state and action.
Manrope for human-readable hierarchy; JetBrains Mono for instrument labels and evidence links.
Hairlines, tonal layers, and alignment create depth without shadows.
Real project, résumé, service, blog, and email destinations remain the source of truth.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is a state and action signal, not decoration. Keep it concentrated on actions, active tabs, progress, links, and focus.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Every visual claim should resolve to existing project, service, résumé, blog, or contact evidence; do not add unsupported outcomes or performance claims.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: Use Manrope for hierarchy and explanation; use JetBrains Mono only where a compact readout or evidence affordance helps scanning.

rules.name: The Compressed Display Rule
rules.body: Large headings carry negative tracking only at the established display/headline sizes; body text remains open and readable.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest; hierarchy is earned through tone, border, spacing, and alignment.

rules.name: The Line Before Lift Rule
rules.body: When a boundary or state needs emphasis, strengthen the hairline or apply the cobalt state before considering any additional material effect.

dos: Do lead with Fisher Lok’s existing identity, services, experience, projects, writing, and email destination.
Do use the calibrated signal path to explain the research-to-deployment range.
Do keep Manrope and JetBrains Mono in their established display/body versus instrument-label roles.
Do use cobalt for action, active state, links, progress, and focus; keep its area intentionally limited.
Do preserve line-led, no-shadow tonal depth and the 1020px, 760px, and 520px responsive behavior.
Do honor keyboard focus, semantic tab behavior, and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
donts: Don't introduce bookstore/editorial warmth, parchment, brick-red, or gold.
Don't imitate Apple or reuse Apple-like product-gallery language.
Don't turn the site into generic SaaS cards, a fake terminal, or a dashboard.
Don't add cyberpunk glow, gradients, decorative shadows, or ornamental glass effects.
Don't fabricate clients, testimonials, trading returns, performance figures, deployments, or commercial outcomes.
Don't replace evidence rows or the blog list with empty marketing claims.
